BCI.definition: System that translates neural activity into commands for external devices (or vice versa)

FIH.definition: First time a device is implanted in or used on a human subject

BDD.definition: US FDA program granting priority review and interaction for devices treating serious conditions

IDE.definition: US FDA approval to use an unapproved device in a clinical study

TAP.expansion: Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program
TAP.definition: US FDA pilot providing early strategic engagement across a device's life cycle

JV.definition: Business entity jointly owned by two or more partner companies

FDA.definition: US regulator for medical devices and drugs

NMPA.definition: China's medical device and drug regulator

EEG.definition: Non-invasive recording of the brain's electrical activity via scalp electrodes

MEA.definition: Grid of tiny electrodes for recording/stimulating neural tissue at high resolution

DBS.definition: Implanted electrodes delivering electrical stimulation to deep brain structures

TMS.definition: Non-invasive brain stimulation via magnetic pulses through the skull

tDCS.definition: Non-invasive brain stimulation via weak direct electrical current

tES.definition: Umbrella term for non-invasive electrical brain stimulation methods

VNS.definition: Electrical stimulation of the vagus nerve for therapeutic effect

taVNS.definition: Non-invasive VNS delivered via the ear

FES.definition: Electrical stimulation of nerves/muscles to restore movement

fNIRS.definition: Non-invasive brain imaging via blood-oxygenation changes measured with infrared light

fMRI.definition: Brain imaging measuring activity via blood-flow changes

MRI.definition: Structural imaging using magnetic fields and radio waves

MEG.definition: Brain imaging via magnetic fields produced by neural currents

OPM-MEG.definition: Wearable MEG using quantum optical sensors

sEMG.definition: Non-invasive recording of muscle electrical activity from the skin

EMG.definition: Recording of electrical activity in muscles

ERP.definition: Brain response time-locked to a stimulus measured with EEG

ECoG.definition: Recording of brain activity from electrodes placed on the cortical surface

PNS.definition: Nerves outside the brain and spinal cord

TBI.definition: Brain injury from external mechanical force

SCI.definition: Damage to the spinal cord causing loss of function

ALS.definition: Progressive neurodegenerative disease affecting motor neurons

AR.definition: Digital content overlaid on the physical world

SDK.definition: Toolset for building software against a platform

OEM.definition: Company whose components are used in another company's end products

CMOS.definition: Chip technology used in high-density neural interfaces

CE.definition: EU regulatory marking for products including medical devices

PMA.definition: Most stringent US FDA approval pathway for high-risk devices

510(k).definition: US FDA pathway clearing devices substantially equivalent to existing ones

SCS.definition: Electrical stimulation of the spinal cord for chronic pain or motor restoration

ExG.definition: Umbrella for surface bioelectrical signals (EEG, EMG, ECG, EOG)

sEEG.definition: Depth electrodes recording intracranial EEG to localize epileptic zones

(f)MRI.definition: Structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging

ECG.definition: Recording of the heart's electrical activity

EFS.definition: A small first-in-human study to evaluate a device's basic safety and function

Pivotal.definition: Late-stage clinical study intended to support a marketing application

trial.definition: A formal study of a device or therapy in human subjects

HUD.definition: FDA rare-disease device designation enabling an HDE marketing application; designation alone is not marketing approval
